rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a blastocyst with visible ICM and peripheral TE, but overstates expansion and compatibility with 3AA from this image; the blastocoel does not clearly occupy most of the embryo and TE cohesion/quality are harder to confirm than described.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, day of transfer, endometrial thickness, BMI, prior cycle history, and semen parameters well, with appropriate discussion of favorable and cautionary factors, though some links are somewhat generic.

Reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a plausible prognosis tied to embryo and patient factors; minor issues include somewhat speculative weighting of stress/alcohol and image-based confidence.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET for a good-prognosis 34-year-old, caution about overinterpreting one failed transfer, and optional rather than routine PGT-A. Minor deviations include overemphasis on lifestyle factors for immediate implantation odds.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support adherence, activity guidance, and future evaluation if failure occurs; useful though not highly individualized beyond standard care.
